accepted_edits.reason: the edits restate §10's cause as unknown with a note naming it, replace its negative control, and narrow §11 to the scope check, as the read-back's findings asked

findings.reason: a node sent to build lane selection that already exists would not reproduce the reported symptom, and would repair the wrong mechanism instead of whatever leaves a held metered launch never resolving.
findings.text: §10's Why says "the only admission service on the fleet runs `crew admit --lane clive`, so nothing ever takes a request routed to a metered lane", but `admit_once`'s lane filter includes every metered route on the local drainer: for `--lane <local_backend>` it admits each pointer whose backend differs from the lane, with the comment "The installed local drainer also admits every metered route" (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:5285-5298`, present since 1f0303dbdd on 2026-10-27), and a metered launch that a `BudgetHold` stops is recorded on the pointer via `_record_metered_hold` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:5630-5633`); the cited evidence, an empty `admission_history`, is consistent with no attempt only because that key is written solely when a launched pointer carried queued-life facts (`_archive_queued_life`, `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:5897-5911`), so it does not establish the stated cause

findings.reason: the node would record a green red-arm as proof its guard fires, when the declared mutation leaves metered admission untouched; the red arm must remove the metered route from the pass (or refuse it in the stubbed launcher), not narrow the lane.
findings.text: §10's negative control says that limiting admission to the local lane "leaves all three queued with no attempt", but restricting the pass to the local lane is precisely the selection that includes every metered request (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:5290-5298`), so the declared red arm is the positive arm and the mutation it applies changes nothing about metered requests

findings.reason: a worker reading the deliverable literally may re-open the contract composition §2 already closed and re-derive refusals the batch path already applies, spending the node on parity instead of the one check that is missing.
findings.text: §11's deliverable requires a batch entry to be refused "for every reason a direct dispatch of the same node would refuse it", which is the goal §2 already landed, while its done-when measures only the write-scope check, so the node's stated endpoint is wider than the gate that closes it

findings.reason: the worker must either strip the queue-time wrapper to make the texts equal (changing a caller the section did not scope) or weaken the assertion to the finding text, and neither is what the section says; naming "the same refusal finding" rather than the same raised text settles it in one line.
findings.text: §11's done-when requires both refusals to carry "the same reason", but the batch path raises `"node {id!r} is refused at queue time: " + findings` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:349-351`) while the direct dispatch raises the finding text itself (`reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:880`), so literal text equality cannot hold and the assertion the section names is unattainable as written

findings.reason: the plan understates its own cost by 30%, and this declaration has already been carried wrong twice after sections were added, so it will keep drifting unless it is set to the sections' sum.
findings.text: `plan-effort-hours` is 7.0 while the eleven section records sum to 10.0 (0.25 + 0.75 + 1.0 + 1.0 + 1.0 + 0.5 + 1.0 + 0.75 + 0.75 + 2.0 + 1.0), so adding §10 and §11 left the declaration three hours short

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited `a-queue-holds-the-whole-plan` §15 resolves and carries the metered-launch promise, and every module a write path names exists (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py`, `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py`).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §10's done-when declares a negative control that cannot go red, because limiting admission to the local lane is exactly the selection that admits every metered request (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:5285-5298`).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections put every log under the run directory and site their deliverables in `tests/`, which survives the run.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test filenames and the section prose carry no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §10's stated root cause is contradicted by the code it blames, and §11's deliverable claims a parity its own measure cannot check.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §10 names one deliverable (a metered request launches or is refused with a reason) and §11 names one (a batch entry faces the write-scope refusal), each reviewable on one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §10 cites `a-queue-holds-the-whole-plan` §15, which exists and records the promise it is: §15 is titled "a ready metered request launches at once" and is `done`, so no unlanded dependency is left undeclared; §11's dependency on §2 is already `done` and so needs no queue ordering.
